observation: Heading and body typeface differ completely. A uses the custom sans 'Graphik' on all 196 measured elements. B uses Georgia serif (71 elements) for headings and body, with system-ui (60 elements) for nav, buttons and attributions.
evidence: A fonts_by_element_count: Graphik 196. B: Georgia 71, system-ui 60. B h1 font-family is Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif.

observation: The h1 is much larger and heavier-looking in A. It has very tight tracking and a bold geometric sans look. B's h1 is a smaller serif.
evidence: A h1 76.56px, weight 700, Graphik. B h1 64px, weight 700, Georgia.

observation: The h2 size is much smaller in B than in A, which flattens the heading hierarchy.
evidence: A h2 58px vs B h2 41.6px.

observation: Body text is larger in A (23.2px with line-height equal to the font size, i.e. 1.0). B uses 18px with a 28.8px line-height (1.6), so its paragraphs read looser and more conventional.
evidence: A body_font_size 23.2px, body_line_height 23.2px. B 18px / 28.8px.

observation: The page background differs. A is stark white with a beige wavy hand-drawn band behind the project mockup. B uses a warm cream background across the page.
evidence: A body_bg rgb(255,255,255), with rgb(251,247,240) only in sub-areas. B body_bg rgb(251,248,241).

observation: The primary CTA changes from a flat, square, bright yellow rectangle in A to a pill-shaped, muted golden-amber button with a shadow in B.
evidence: A bg rgb(255,224,0) with 0 border-radius. B primary_button bg rgb(233,183,43), radius 999px, padding 16px 34px, text colour rgb(34,34,34).

observation: A's header has two outlined/filled boxed buttons: a bordered 'Sign in' and a dark-navy filled 'Try it FREE'. B shows 'Sign in' as a plain text link and 'Try it FREE' as a small yellow pill.
evidence: A screenshot: boxed 'Sign in' (transparent bg, radius 0) and dark 'Try it FREE'. B screenshot: plain 'Sign in', pill 'Try it FREE'.

observation: The logo is rendered differently. A inlines it as one SVG with a dark navy outline mark and wordmark. B uses an external basecamp-logo.svg image with a yellow-filled mark, at 137x38.
evidence: A svgs: 1, img count 5. B images list basecamp-logo.svg at 137x38 and has 0 inline svgs.

observation: A's navigation sits flush at the far edges of a full-width bar, with the logo at x≈24. B constrains the header to a centred container, with the logo at x=140.
evidence: A screenshot: logo at left edge. B facts: logo rect x=140.

observation: A has two h1 elements, the second one empty, which is a heading-structure flaw. B has a single clean h1.
evidence: A h1_count 2 and heading_outline ends with a level-1 entry with empty text. B h1_count 1.

observation: A has two nav elements, 41 anchors, 22 divs and 13 script tags. B is much leaner: 1 nav, 31 anchors, 11 divs and 0 scripts.
evidence: A tag_counts: nav 2, a 41, div 22, script 13. B: nav 1, a 31, div 11, no script.

observation: A carries extensive head metadata: OG/Twitter tags, theme-color, robots, 2 JSON-LD blocks, and 13 meta tags with 3 stylesheets. B has only charset and viewport, no JSON-LD, and zero external stylesheets (one inline style).

observation: A has no ARIA attributes in B's sense of the word: A has 3 aria attributes and B has none. B has fewer accessibility hooks.
